title: Foray engine parity fixture (plan §6.2)
description: One file under player/parity/fixtures/<family>/. Read in place by the JS runner (player/parity/runner.js) and by the Swift ForayEngineParity library. JS is the reference: record.mjs writes every non-authored `expect` from the real JS module. The enums in $defs are the CLOSED sets both runners check; runner.js reads them from this file rather than restating them.

module.description: Repo-relative path of the JS module every read/call case in this file targets. Required when the file has read or call cases.

note.description: Free text for a human reader. Never read by a runner.

jsOnly.description: true: the family pins a JS rule that is deliberately never ported to Swift: plan §5.5 C-2's continuation hops (computed by the page, only walked by the engine), and since NE-39s manager-await (the JS manager's awaits: a load parked on the synthesiser's pause, onStateSettled per _handle frame, which a synchronous native turn does not have; each case's note names the XCTest holding the native form). The Swift and JVM runners skip these files by this flag and no book may owe their ids. Every file of a family must agree.

nativeOnly.description: code-health-3 CH3-20: true: the family pins the native cores' own episode path at the wheel (native-episode): what a raw MPRemoteCommand press, the deck's load deadline, a grace expiry and a relinquish do, asserted on the n.* tokens (compare.js NATIVE_TOKEN_FAMILIES keeps them). The JS reference has none of these inputs (no toggle press, no load deadline, no background task, no relinquish), so the JS runner validates these files and NEVER runs them, and record.mjs never records them: every case is authored, its expect written from the Swift core (EngineCore through ForayEngineParity's scenario driver) and held by engine-parity, and the JVM ParitySuite is held to the same expects. Such a family is in jvm-pending.json "runs", never owed whole. Every file of a family must agree; a file is never both jsOnly and nativeOnly.

caseId.description: <family>/<slug>. Unique across every fixture file. Never reused for a different rule: parity-report.json and jvm-pending.json refer to cases by id (as swift-pending.json did until NE-39s).

coversEntry.description: <suite stem>::<exact top-level test() name> — the JS test this case stands for in coverage.test.js.

authored.description: true: the expect was written by a person from the spec, and record.mjs refuses to overwrite it. A JS change that disagrees with an authored case is refused, not re-recorded.

read.description: An exported constant of the file's module.

call.description: An exported function of the file's module.

tolerance.description: Absolute tolerance for finite numbers in the comparison. Absent = exact. Never applies to $num tags.

thrown.description: The rule under test threw. Only the class is compared: a message is text, and text is pinned by the JS suites (exclusion reason text-pin), not by parity.

opLog.description: Ordered op tokens. Backend tokens are queue-manager.test.js's FakeBackend grammar, unchanged: load:<id>@<s>, play, pause, seek:<s>, outPoint:<s|null>, rate:<r>, release. Other adapters are prefixed: tts.*, interlude.*, store.*, preview.* (NE-47: the engine's preview deck, preview.load:<url>, preview.play, preview.stop). NE-39j, manager target: prefetch:<id>@<s> (the manager's ask to warm the next item, setup.backend.prefetch), event.settled:<state> (setup.settledEvents), telemetry:<line> (setup.telemetry). Native-only tokens are n.* and are stripped before comparison except in the prepare, prepare-narration and native-episode families (compare.js NATIVE_TOKEN_FAMILIES).

target.description: What the scenario drives. JS drivers exist for: manager, deck (NE-28j: the outpoint family over deck-policy.js outPointStep and a driven clock), and engine (NE-30j: the prepare family over player/parity/reference-engine.js with the warm handover on; call steps are engine commands, deck steps its deck events, and every checkpoint carries nowMs, the T of an audible start).

positionEvents.description: NE-14j: the manager's position store is the real PositionStore, and its onSave writes event.position:<id>@<seconds>:<duration> into the op log (plan §5.5 pendingEvents).

backend.description: FakeBackend options (fakes.js): failLoadFor, durationById, duration, holdLoads, loadTurns; NE-39j, manager target: prefetch (true, or "loses": the web lane's prefetch contract, whose ask is the op prefetch:<id>@<s>, and a deck "window" step to open it), coldLoadMs (a load with nothing warm waits that long on the manual clock), slowFirstPlay (the first play settles only at the next pause).

catalogue.description: The Foray resolver's table: item_id -> episode row.

tts.description: The narration bridge (fakes.js fakeTts). An object opts into NE-31j's shapes: refuse, voiceFallback, onFinished: false, transport: false, pause: rejects, resume: {answer}, state: true; NE-39j: pause: held (answered by a tts releasePause step).

voice.description: NE-31j, manager target: the listener's chosen narration voice the manager is constructed with (null: the synthesiser picks).

narrationTicks.description: NE-31j, manager target: wire the surface's narration pulse (onNarrationTick), counted for the narrationTicks view. The manager runs its narration ticker, and so its deadline, only when a surface listens.

view.description: NE-30j, manager target: extra checkpoint fields, opt-in (runner.js VIEW_KEYS).

settledEvents.description: NE-39j, manager target: the surface's settled-state hook (onStateSettled) writes event.settled:<state> into the op log after every handled event.

telemetry.description: NE-39j, manager target: telemetry lines recorded as telemetry:<line>, by event name from the closed runner.js TELEMETRY_EVENTS (rate.snapped).

seamGapEvents.description: NE-30j, manager target: the surface beat callback writes event.seamGap:<true|false> into the op log.

forayBuild.description: NE-30j, manager target: a real curated Foray built as the page builds it ({id, data: frozen | committed, dropSources?, segments?: false}); a playForay or setQueueFromForay call with no args plays its hydrated document.

capabilities.description: NE-30j, engine target: what the reference engine advertises (default: episode, continuation, restore, foray).

preview.description: NE-47, engine target: the preview deck a rendered audition plays on (fakes.js fakePreview). failUrls: urls whose load fails, so the audition is spoken instead.

verb.description: The closed scenario verbs (plan §6.2). Every verb has a JS driver; a verb added without one fails with E_NO_JS_DRIVER naming the card that adds it (runner.js PENDING_DRIVERS). session and lifecycle (NE-14j) take the values in runner.js SESSION_EVENTS and LIFECYCLE_EVENTS; remote (NE-29j) takes an action from runner.js REMOTE_ACTIONS, with optional details (seekto's {seekTime}), pressed through media-session.js mediaSessionActions; with raw: true (CH3-20) it takes a native remote command from runner.js RAW_REMOTE_COMMANDS instead (the MPRemoteCommand a head unit, a headset or the lock screen delivers, togglePlayPause among them), with an optional value (changePlaybackPosition's target, which it requires; a skip's value is the head unit's interval, which the step ignores), delivered as that command and never through the action table.

step.description: Exactly one verb key, plus that verb's own fields (args, await, reason, message, sec, audible, id, shouldResume, routeName, isCarRoute, items, index, autoplay, details; for the deck target, outPointSec, rate and token, and the ended event; NE-30j: a call step may carry returns, a runner.js RETURN_PROJECTIONS name, and on the engine target refused; NE-31j: a manager-target clock step may carry every (advance in steps of that many ms, an awake page), and the tts verb takes finish or silent; NE-39j: it also takes releasePause, and a manager-target deck step may be window; CH3-20, the native drivers only (a nativeOnly family): a manager-target deck step may be deadline (the deck's load deadline, .deadlineExceeded for the load in flight, optional afterMs, default 20000), and a lifecycle step may be graceExpired (the background task's expiration handler) or relinquish (the page's relinquish command, optional cap, default all)).

macro.description: Input-only shorthands, each the ONLY key of its object. $seg: [id, start=100, end=210, extra?] -> {id, kind:'episode', start_sec, end_sec, ...extra}. $ep: [id, extra?] -> {id, kind:'episode', ...extra}. $tts: [id, extra?] -> {id, kind:'tts', ...extra}. $foray: '<committed id in data/forays.json>' | {id, title?, items[]}.

special.description: Values JSON cannot carry, each the ONLY key of its object. Legal in inputs and in expects.

input.description: Any JSON, with macros and specials expanded by the runner.

encoded.description: Any JSON, with specials as $num/$undefined tags and object keys sorted. Never a macro.

harnessError.description: Codes a runner raises when a CASE is malformed, as opposed to the rule under test throwing. Both runners use these codes.
